newsitem.title: JAPAN: Key JGBs end sharply down in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Key JGBs end sharply down in Tokyo.

text.p: Key March Japanese government bond futures ended sharply down on Wednesday.
"There are no obvious reasons to sell, but the March inched gradually downwards," a trust bank trader said.
There were rumours that public funds had sold cash JGBs, traders said.
Some say public funds are selling in small lots, while others say they have made large-lot sales, a trader for a trust bank's securities unit said.
However, such selling could not be confirmed, the trader added.
The March ended at 125.24, down from Tuesday's 125.51.
Turnover was 37,959 contracts.
There was a rumour in the bond market that a city bank had lost 100 billion yen in derivatives trading, which might be causing of some JGB selling, a brokerage trader said.
The rumour could not immediately be confirmed.
Although cash JGBs were sold on Wednesday, cash bonds should continue to find support from a tight supply and demand balance in the near term, traders said.
Later this month, the JGB market anticipates some cash flow from the government's scheme to wind up failed mortgage firms.
Under the scheme, agricultural financial institutions are expected to receive some 2.7 trillion yen by December 20.
Market players expect some portion of the funds to flow toward bonds.
Comments made by the Bank of Japan governor Yasuo Matsushita to a parliamentary budget committee on Wednesday had little effect on the market, the second trader said.
Matsushita said that it was important to lead the Japanese economy to a situation where it could achieve sustainable growth.
Matsushita also said the economic recovery is gradual, but there are "various" moves in the economy which are showing a firmer recovery.
There was talk, wide-spread in the market, that a high-ranking government official has allegedly received 600 million yen in bribes from a stock speculator.
The talk could not be confirmed immediately.
"The talk led to a fall in stock prices, which invited initial buying of JGBs, but JGBs proved heavy on the upperside from there," the first trader said.
The yield of the benchmark 182nd JGB stood at 2.470 percent as of 0724 GMT, up from previous day's 2.425 percent.
-- Masayuki Kitano, Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-5473-3748
